extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors involved in scholarly peer review (especially those interested in structured peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: A peer-review history page for a research article reporting a pilot of structured peer review; includes reviewer and editor criteria and guidance covering reporting, experimental design, methods/statistics, instrument design, and editorial process requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript language, clarity, grammar, and reporting should be checked by a fluent English speaker to ensure correct use of indefinite/definite articles, tense, sentence structure, and flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: rewrite awkward/tense-mismatched sentence to past tense and improve flow (example: 'Web of Science data from June 2023 ... indicated that the mean word count ... was 368 words (no SD provided)'). Address many instances of missing articles and awkward parenthetical constructions. Specific line-level examples are provided (e.g., lines 264-266, 197, 208, 238, 241). PeerJ can provide language editing services (contact [email protected]) or authors should make their own arrangements and report this in the response letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: The pilot study design should be clear and permit assessment of how structured peer review changes reviewer behavior; study scope and comparisons must be explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer suggests comparing final reviewer recommendations after structured review vs before implementation to assess whether structured reports affect reviewers' final suggestions to editors. Clarify whether previously reviewers were free-format (i.e., whether editors required any form prior to the pilot) instead of leaving readers to assume it. The pilot is a 'great start' but future studies should test appropriateness and quality of structured reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — clarity of sample/phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological descriptions must be unambiguous (e.g., clarify phrasing such as 'to 5 first manuscripts' and define what 'first manuscript' means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise sentences in the Methods to use language similar to what authors used in the response letter. Ensure that clarifications mentioned in the response letter are also inserted into the revised manuscript where appropriate (PeerJ Staff Note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analyses — reporting and post-hoc tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods should be fully reported, including which post-hoc tests were used after omnibus tests (e.g., Kruskal–Wallis), and statistical output files should include those post-hoc results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line 215: state which post-hoc test (Conover’s, perhaps) was used to assess pairwise differences between disciplines and IF quartiles. Provide revised statistical output documents where post-hoc results are present. Note: MedCalc automatically provides Conover’s post-hoc tests but those results were not present in the provided outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting — abbreviations and confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical terms and measures should be clearly defined and their abbreviations stated; confidence intervals and abbreviations should be reported appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines 217-218 — state the abbreviation for odds ratio (OR) and indicate that 95% confidence intervals (CI) are described for them. Define 'Md' and 'IQR' at first use as 'Median (Md)' and 'interquartile range (IQR)'. Spell out 'stat.' to 'statistical' where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor/editorial corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix small textual, formatting, and typographical errors identified in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: change 'Non Applicable' to 'Not Applicable' (Line 151), change 'NA' to 'N/A' (Line 192), change 'reviewers' to 'reviewers’' where possession is intended (Lines 194 and 353), make verbs past tense where needed (Line 195), correct pluralization (e.g., 'Satisfactions' → 'Satisfaction', Line 332). Many line-specific minor corrections are enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response letter and manuscript edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must address all reviewer and editorial comments in a response letter, and any edits or clarifications mentioned in that letter should also be inserted into the revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ Staff Note: ensure all review and editorial comments are addressed in a response letter and that any edits/clarifications mentioned in the letter are also inserted into the revised manuscript where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured review instrument design — question format consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of the structured review questions should be consistent and appropriate for the question type (e.g., choose drop-down vs yes/no where suitable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic Editor: 'Given that questions 2,3, and 5 were also yes/no/Non-applicable, why weren't those questions implemented as drop-downs, like question 9?' Consider implementing consistent UI/response formats (drop-downs vs yes/no/N/A) across comparable items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of free-text responses to refine instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze free-text answers from reviewers to identify possible revisions or extensions to the structured review instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic Editor asked: 'Did the analysis of the free-text answers suggest any possible revisions or extensions to the structured review?' Authors should report whether free-text analysis informed instrument changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review / reviewer identification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy about reviewer naming and public acknowledgment: reviewers are encouraged (but not required) to provide names; if they do, their profile shows public acknowledgment and, if article accepted, their name associates with the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: 'Peer reviewers are encouraged (but not required) to provide their names to the authors when submitting their peer review. If they agree to provide their name, then their personal profile page will reflect a public acknowledgment that they performed a review (even if the article is rejected). If the article is accepted, then reviewers who provided their name will be associated with the article itself.' Link to 'examples of open peer review' is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of review history
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews of published articles are made public, including manuscript files, peer review comments, author rebuttals and revised materials (with a noted date exception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: This openness was optional for articles submitted before 13 February 2023. The review history page makes available versioned editorial decisions, reviewer reviews, and authors' response letters, and indicates number of reviewers and editor involvement per version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recommendations and editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review outcomes and editorial decisions should be clearly reported (e.g., Minor Revisions, Accept) along with editor commentary about outstanding concerns to be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic Editor comments include specific actionable items (e.g., request to revise ambiguous phrasing in Methods). The decision history shows which versions were reviewed, by whom, and the decisions (Minor Revisions → Accept).
